## How is AI security priced?

 AI security is sold on four pricing models, and they are not comparable line for line. Per-seat pricing scales with the humans on your team, per-agent with the number of agents you run, per-request with how busy those agents are, and platform pricing bundles agent controls into a larger security contract with an annual minimum. The same workload can differ by an order of magnitude depending on which model a vendor uses, which is why a quoted number means very little until you know what it counts. 

| Pricing model | What it counts | Best when | Where it bites |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Per seat | Named human users of the console | A small security team oversees many agents | It prices your headcount, not your risk. Adding agents costs nothing, so the number stops describing exposure |
| Per agent | Distinct agents under policy | You run a countable fleet with clear owners | Multi-agent designs inflate the count fast, and definitions of one agent vary between vendors |
| Per request or per action | Calls inspected or authorized | Traffic is spiky or you are piloting | A chatty agent can multiply the bill overnight, and you cannot forecast before you have observed |
| Platform bundle | A larger security contract with AI included | You already buy the platform | Annual minimums, usually well into six figures, and agent depth varies by module maturity |

 We price per agent, published above, because it is the number that tracks what you are actually asking us to govern and it is the one you can forecast before signing. The honest caveat is that per-agent pricing is the least flattering model for heavily multi-agent architectures, so if you run swarms of short-lived sub-agents, tell us and we will scope it properly rather than counting every ephemeral worker. 

 For the full cost picture, including the engineering time teams spend building controls in-house before they buy anything, see our breakdown of what AI agent security costs. If you are still shortlisting, the AI agent security companies guide covers who sells what and which specialists now sit inside larger platforms. 

## Pricing questions, answered.

 What does it cost? 

Agentshield has transparent, self-serve pricing with real prices on the pricing page, starting at $49 per month on the Developer plan, $199 per month on Team (the most popular), and $749 per month on Scale, with Enterprise priced by volume. There is no contact-sales wall to learn the cost, which is part of the wedge: you should not have to book a call to find out what an agent security tool costs.

 Can I run it on-prem, self-hosted, or in my VPC? 

Yes, on higher tiers. On-prem, private cloud, and VPC deployments are available on Scale and Enterprise plans for teams with data-residency or isolation requirements. Reach out through the contact page and a security engineer will scope the deployment with you.

 Which agent stacks does it support? 

Agentshield is stack-neutral. It drops in front of OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, CrewAI, MCP servers, and custom agents as a control plane, so there is no framework rewrite. It sits in the request and action path rather than replacing your agent framework, which means you keep the stack you already built and add firewall, permissions, monitoring, and audit in front of it.

 Is this just a prompt-injection filter or another wrapper? 

No. Agentshield is four controls in one plane, not a single guardrail. It combines a prompt-injection firewall, tool and data permissions, real-time monitoring, and an immutable audit trail, so you get the firewall plus least-privilege plus observability plus the audit evidence without stitching together three vendors. It is the control layer in front of your agent, not a single point tool you bolt on.
